A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sliding Tile Attention work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; the additional page in v2 reflects reflow rather than missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original kernel benchmarks, HunyuanVideo generation experiments, human evaluations, and FLUX image-superresolution results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original kernel, video-generation, human-evaluation, and image-superresolution experiments and reports revised training-free results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 substantially revises training-free mask selection: sparsity-ordered thresholding of whole-model output error becomes minimum-error selection using per-head attention outputs. It also reserves the initial T0 diffusion steps for full attention. The underlying tile-attention mechanism, kernel design, and finetuning losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HunyuanVideo evaluation on VBench and MovieGen prompts, synthetic training videos using Mixkit prompts, and FLUX superresolution on COCO-2014 captions. The sampling-step scenarios and qualitative-example prompts are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: FA2/FA3, CLEAR, NATTEN/Tiled NATTEN, Swin, and Δ-DiT retain their comparison roles. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 specifies the revised STA configuration: full attention for the first 12, 6, and 3 steps of 50-, 25-, and 10-step inference, respectively, replacing Algorithm 1's previous search across all steps. Sampling-step counts, scheduler shifts, metrics, and the 200-prompt human-evaluation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing sampling-step robustness study in Table 3 is revised for the changed STA procedure, altering its sensitivity findings. Figures 6, 10, and 11 replace STA examples for retained prompts. No new ablation questions are introduced, and Appendix E's sparsity and VBench-component analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains attention-recall averages and standard deviations across 10 prompts. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Updated human-preference percentages do not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Training-free results are substantially replaced. At 50 steps, Table 3 changes STA latency from 695s to 501s and SSIM/PSNR/CD-FVD from 76.21/19.94/97.03 to 87.67/28.76/66.12. At 10 steps, CD-FVD instead worsens from 80.41 to 84.80. Figure 7 changes STA's win rate against Δ-DiT from 58.5% to 66.5% and its tie rate against HunyuanVideo from 74.5% to 83.0%. These concern revised STA configurations, not isolated same-setting gains; kernel, finetuning, and appendix quantitative tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2, their assumptions and block-count formulas, Equations 1–5, and Appendix A's attention-mask definitions are unchanged. Algorithm 1's procedural revision does not introduce new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens the training-free latency claim from 685s to 501s while retaining the claim of no quality degradation. The introduction raises the reported FA3 training-free speedup to 1.89×. The central locality, hardware-efficiency, novelty, and finetuning contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 removes the explanation that caching becomes less effective at low step counts because temporal redundancy diminishes. It replaces the interpretation of a narrow structural-similarity gap with discussion of both structural and detail degradation in Δ-DiT across sampling budgets. Complementarity with caching and distillation remains in the conclusion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a FastVideo code-access link, specifies averaging mask-search losses over 16 prompts, and provides exact initial full-attention step counts. The 16-prompt count is newly disclosed, not evidence of an increased calibration sample. Appendix training hyperparameters, hardware, and baseline implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to DistFlashAttn, FasterCache, and Pyramid Attention Broadcast alongside the initial-full-attention procedure in Section 3.2. The main related-work discussion and research positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the abstract, introduction, training-free method description, and Sections 4.2–4.3. Section and appendix organization is retained, and the preprint notice becomes an ICML proceedings notice.

P2.justification: Figure 7 is updated and relabeled; Figures 6, 10, and 11 refresh STA panels and labels, with runtime annotations added to the appendix galleries. Table 3's caption and SSIM formatting change. Core diagrams and other table structures remain intact, with modest page reflow.

improvement.justification: The explicit calibration and initial-full-attention details, added code-access information, and updated quantitative and visual evidence make the revised training-free procedure easier to assess and reproduce. The 501s headline also agrees with Table 3, resolving v1's 685s-versus-695s discrepancy. Gains are qualified: 10-step CD-FVD worsens, and more human-evaluation ties do not establish identical quality. These support a limited overall improvement while the core kernel, theory, and finetuning evidence remain intact.
